linger:Café de la Comédie.name: Le Grand Café du Théâtre
linger:Café de la Comédie.teaser: A brasserie bar facing the town theatre since 1847: coffee at the counter, the square going past
linger:Café de la Comédie.story: The old guide put a café under a theatre colonnade on the Place de la Comédie. There is no theatre there now: the square kept the name of a small playhouse of the Revolution years, long demolished. The real theatre stands at the head of the Place de la Liberté, and the café that has faced it since 1847 is the Grand Café du Théâtre, on the corner of rue Jean Jaurès. Expect a long brasserie room with a bar, a terrace, regulars reading the paper over a coffee, and at noon the clatter of steak-frites, tartare and mussels going out.
linger:Café de la Comédie.why: Take the morning coffee at the bar before the Thursday market fills the squares, then walk to Pelen on rue Blaise Pascal for something sweet.
facts: Where
2 rue Jean Jaurès, opposite the theatre at the top of the Place de la Liberté
Open
Kitchen 12:00 to 14:00 (Sat 14:30) and 19:00 to 22:00 (Fri and Sat 22:30) per Jura Tourisme (Oct 2026); a directory gives the bar Mon to Sat 07:30 to 23:30, closed Sunday (not confirmed)
Order
A coffee at the bar mid-morning; a brasserie plate at lunch
Work?
Fine for a coffee and a few emails outside meal hours; no wifi confirmed, and at noon it is a working brasserie, not a laptop room

linger:The Médiathèque.name: Médiathèque 4C
linger:The Médiathèque.teaser: Free reading rooms and wifi inside the old Cordeliers convent quarter, a step off the market squares
linger:The Médiathèque.story: When the arcades are too loud, the public library of the Lons agglomeration is the quiet answer. It sits in the 4C, the Centre culturel communautaire des Cordeliers on rue des Cordeliers, the same block as the Franciscan church that gives the street its name and a cinema that shares the building. Inside: tables, newspapers and magazines on racks, students with headphones, the hush of a municipal reading room. Nobody asks you to buy anything, and Jura Tourisme lists wifi among the services, so a chef can sit down with a laptop and sort the week's orders.
linger:The Médiathèque.why: The one free, quiet table in the centre with wifi; pair it with a look into the Église des Cordeliers next door.

drink:Vin Jaune.name: Vin Jaune
drink:Vin Jaune.teaser: Savagnin left under a skin of yeast for six years, then sold in a bottle that holds only 62 cl
drink:Vin Jaune.story: Vin Jaune is Savagnin put into old barrels and never topped up. As the wine evaporates, a film of yeast, the voile, spreads over its surface and keeps it from turning to vinegar while letting a little air through. It stays there for more than six years; producers count six years and three months from harvest before it may leave the cellar. What survives from a litre is roughly 62 cl, the size of the squat clavelin it must be sold in. The smell is the molecule sotolon, isolated from fenugreek in 1975: walnut, curry, maple syrup. Open it an hour ahead and serve it cool, not cold.
drink:Vin Jaune.why: Order one glass with a wedge of old Comté before the poularde arrives; the walnut in both makes the case for the whole region.
facts: In the glass

Deep gold; walnut, curry, dried apple and spice from sotolon (about 120 to 268 µg per litre in published analyses); dry, sharp, very long. A thinner voile than Sherry's flor, at lower alcohol, and never fortified
On the label
Château-Chalon (Vin Jaune only) or Vin Jaune under Arbois, Côtes du Jura or L'Étoile; always the 62 cl clavelin, and a vintage at least six years back
Ask for

A glass to taste before buying, then a clavelin from a named house such as Macle at Château-Chalon or Tissot at Arbois; about EUR 35 to 90 a clavelin (seen May 2026). Savagnin's ancestry is its own card

drink:Poulsard and Trousseau.name: Poulsard and Trousseau
drink:Poulsard and Trousseau.teaser: Two native reds: one pale enough to read through, the other dark, firm and tasting of iron
drink:Poulsard and Trousseau.story: The Jura's own red grapes cover about a fifth of its vines between them, Poulsard (called Ploussard in Pupillin) a little more than Trousseau. Poulsard has thin skins and makes a wine so pale it can pass for a dark rosé: orange-ruby, cranberry and cherry, almost no tannin, bright acid. Pupillin, above Arbois, signs itself the world capital of Ploussard. Trousseau is its opposite, deeper in colour, firmer, black cherry with an iron, peppery edge, and at its best on the gravels around Arbois. Pour them side by side and the Jura's red range is laid out in two glasses.
drink:Poulsard and Trousseau.why: Ask for one of each by the glass at the Caveau des Jacobins and taste the pale one first.
facts: In the glass
Poulsard: translucent orange-ruby, red berries, light and acidic, serve at 12 to 14 °C. Trousseau: darker ruby, black cherry, iron and pepper, more grip, serve at 14 to 16 °C
On the label
Arbois or Arbois-Pupillin, Côtes du Jura, with Poulsard, Ploussard or Trousseau on the label; Tissot's Singulier is a Trousseau
Ask for

Poulsard with Morteau or Morbier; Trousseau with an 18-month Comté or game. Pupillin's Fruitière Vinicole for a village Ploussard; Overnoy-Houillon bottles if a list has one. About EUR 18 to 40 for Poulsard, 22 to 55 for Trousseau (seen May 2026)

sources.label: CIVJ, Vignoble du Jura 2024 infographic

drink:The appellations.name: The Jura appellations
drink:The appellations.teaser: Four place names and three products on about 2,100 ha: the smallest serious vineyard map in France
drink:The appellations.story: The Jura vineyard runs as a thin strip of slope, the Revermont, from south of Lons to north of Arbois, about 2,100 ha in all by the CIVJ's count from 2023 declarations, with some 350 growers and co-operative members. Four appellations name places: Arbois (767 ha, every style), Côtes du Jura (720 ha, the broad regional), L'Étoile (86 ha, whites only) and Château-Chalon (55 ha, Vin Jaune and nothing else). Three name products: Crémant, Macvin and Marc du Jura. Small also means fragile: frost and mildew cut the 2024 harvest by about 71 percent; 2025 came back to normal volumes.
drink:The appellations.why: Learn the four place names before your first cellar; Arbois's 1936 first-gazette story has its own card.
facts: In the glass
Five main grapes: Chardonnay (about 43% of the vines), Savagnin (25%), Pinot Noir, Poulsard and Trousseau. Whites come either topped-up (ouillé, fresh) or under voile (nutty, oxidative)
On the label

Arbois (Arbois-Pupillin for that village), Château-Chalon, Côtes du Jura, L'Étoile; plus Crémant du Jura, Macvin du Jura, Marc du Jura. L'Étoile's name is argued over: the star-shaped crinoid fossils in its soil, or the five hills that ring the village like a star
Ask for
Ouillé or sous voile when you order a white; it changes everything. 9.7 million bottles sold in 2022-23 (CIVJ)

drink:Macvin, Crémant and Marc.name: Macvin, Crémant and Marc
drink:Macvin, Crémant and Marc.teaser: The apéritif made of must and brandy, the everyday sparkling, and the oak-aged digestif
drink:Macvin, Crémant and Marc.story: Three Jura appellations name a product rather than a place. Macvin du Jura, an AOC since 14 November 1991, is a mistelle: unfermented grape must stopped with Marc du Jura, roughly two parts juice to one of brandy, then aged in oak. It comes out sweet, grapey, around 16 percent, and is poured cold before dinner. Crémant du Jura, recognised in 1995, is bottle-fermented sparkling, mostly Chardonnay, nine months at least on its lees: the bubble cellars open at any hour. Marc du Jura, the pomace brandy, became an AOC of its own by decree on 2 February 2015 and closes the meal.
drink:Macvin, Crémant and Marc.why: Start a cellar visit with a Crémant and end it with a thimble of Macvin; it is the Jura's own way into and out of a meal.
facts: In the glass
Macvin: amber or ruby, raisin and walnut, sweet, about 16%. Crémant: fine bubble, apple and brioche, dry. Marc: amber after oak, dried fruit and fire
On the label
Macvin du Jura (blanc, rosé or rouge); Crémant du Jura (brut, often blanc de blancs); Marc du Jura
Ask for
A Macvin as apéritif, a Crémant brut by the glass, a Marc after the cheese; EUR 14 to 35 a bottle (seen May 2026). The Caveau des Jacobins in Lons pours all three

drink:Vin de Paille.name: Vin de Paille
drink:Vin de Paille.teaser: Grapes dried for weeks on straw or in airy lofts, pressed into a few spoonfuls of honeyed wine each
drink:Vin de Paille.story: After harvest, the best bunches of Chardonnay, Savagnin and Poulsard are laid on racks or straw, or hung from the beams of a ventilated loft, and left to shrivel. The rules ask for at least six weeks; many growers wait three months or more, until the must weighs 320 to 420 g of sugar a litre. Pressing gives very little juice. It ferments slowly to at least 14 percent and then ages three years, at least eighteen months of it in wood, before release. It smells of candied orange, quince and honey, with a cut of acidity that keeps it from cloying.
drink:Vin de Paille.why: Ask for it with an old Comté instead of dessert; the salt in the cheese meets the candied fruit.
facts: In the glass
Amber gold; candied orange, dried apricot, quince, honey; sweet but fresh
On the label
Vin de Paille under Arbois, Côtes du Jura or L'Étoile only, usually in a half bottle of 37.5 cl
Ask for
A small glass with Comté, or alone after the meal; about EUR 35 to 65 a half bottle (seen May 2026)

bars:Domaine Macle.name: Domaine Macle
bars:Domaine Macle.teaser: A family cellar on the rock of Château-Chalon, where the Vin Jaune is tasted in the barrel room
bars:Domaine Macle.story: The Macles have farmed Château-Chalon since 1850, from a house on rue de la Roche at the top of the village, the cliff falling away to the Seille below. Laurent Macle took over in 1995 and had the vines certified organic in 2019; in January 2025 his daughter Carmen joined him, back from cellars in New Zealand, Oregon and Meursault. There is no tasting-room theatre: a cold cellar, barrels with their voile, a few glasses. The house is known for Château-Chalon that keeps for decades; in the poor years 1974, 1980, 1984 and 2001 no Château-Chalon was released at all.
bars:Domaine Macle.why: Book ahead and bring cash: a quiet family cellar, and the clearest Château-Chalon lesson on the slope.
facts: Where

Open

bars:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.name: Domaine Stéphane Tissot
bars:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.teaser: The Tissot caveau on Arbois's main square: one of the widest Jura ranges, poured without an appointment
bars:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.story: Bénédicte and Stéphane Tissot farm the family estate, Domaine André et Mireille Tissot, from Montigny-lès-Arsures, the village just north of Arbois where Pasteur kept his vines. The vineyard went organic in 1999 and has been certified biodynamic since 2004; it now runs to more than 46 ha on blue and grey marls, limestone and clay, split into over thirty cuvées. The place to taste is the shop on the Place de la Liberté in Arbois, a few doors from the arcades: Crémant, single-parcel Chardonnays, Trousseau, Vin Jaune and Vin de Paille, a glass of each.
bars:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.why: The easiest serious tasting on the slope: walk in, taste across every Jura style, buy one sous-voile and one topped-up white to compare at home.
facts: Where
Caveau, 35 Place de la Liberté, Arbois; estate at Montigny-lès-Arsures
Open
Tasting at the Arbois caveau (Jura Tourisme, 2024 listing); 2026 winter hours not found: check the website
Pour

Price

Book

bars:Overnoy and Ganevat.name: Overnoy and Ganevat
bars:Overnoy and Ganevat.teaser: Two names natural-wine drinkers fly in for, and why you will meet them on a list, not in their cellars
bars:Overnoy and Ganevat.story: In Pupillin, Pierre Overnoy stopped adding sulphur in 1984 and became the reference for natural wine far beyond the Jura; Emmanuel Houillon, whom he trained, has run the six hectares since 2001. The bottles are allocated years ahead and the house on rue du Ploussard does not run visits. At Rotalier, south of Lons, Jean-François Ganevat sold his family estate in September 2021 to Alexander Pumpyanskiy, a Geneva-based Russian investor. In March 2023 it was bought by Benoît Pontenier and Jocelyn Brancard; Le Monde then reported a money-laundering inquiry and seized assets, with work allowed to go on. Ganevat now bottles with his sister Anne under their names.
bars:Overnoy and Ganevat.why: Do not drive to either door; look for the names on a wine list in Arbois or Lons and order the glass if it appears.
facts: Where
Pupillin (Overnoy-Houillon) and Rotalier (the Ganevat estate); neither is a visit
Open
No public visits or shop found for either (Oct 2026)
Pour
On a few wine lists in the Jura and abroad: a Pupillin Ploussard, a sous-voile Savagnin; the Anne et Jean-François Ganevat labels
Book
Not possible; taste the same grapes from open cellars such as the Fruitière Vinicole de Pupillin or Tissot in Arbois
